en.title: Diablo 5 Officially Announced: A New Era of Terror Dawns on Sanctuary
en.summary: Blizzard has officially unveiled Diablo 5 at BlizzCon 2026, promising a return of the Lord of Terror a century after the events of Diablo 4. The announcement signals a significant shift for the iconic action RPG series, setting its sights on a Spring 2029 release.
en.body:
The long-awaited next chapter in Blizzard Entertainment's legendary dark fantasy series has officially been revealed. At BlizzCon 2026, the studio pulled back the curtain on **Diablo 5**, a brand-new mainline entry that promises to plunge players back into the eternal conflict between Heaven and Hell. The announcement came with a chilling teaser trailer, confirming the return of the primordial demon, the Lord of Terror, himself.

This new installment is set a full century after the cataclysmic events of **Diablo 4**. What sets **Diablo 5** apart is its narrative setting: it will be the first game in the franchise to take place entirely within a post-apocalyptic Sanctuary. This bold move suggests a world irrevocably changed, where the remnants of humanity and demonic forces contend with the ashes of their past. While a precise release date remains under wraps, Blizzard has targeted Spring 2029 for its arrival, a considerable six-year gap since **Diablo 4** launched and over three decades since the series first terrorized players.

## The Future of Sanctuary Unveiled

The BlizzCon 2026 stage was alive with **Diablo** news beyond just the sequel. Fans can look forward to **The Amazon**, a new class pack arriving for **Diablo 4** in 2027, adding another iconic hero to the existing roster. Furthermore, the **Diablo 4 Collection** is slated for release on the Nintendo Switch 2, bringing Blizzard's latest action RPG to Nintendo's next-generation hardware. For those eager to revisit the series' storied past, Season 15 of **Diablo 4** is available now, offering a playable retrospective that spans the franchise's history. The official teaser trailer itself offered a glimpse into the darkness, with a transcript hinting at the return of familiar dread: "The angels were supposed to save us. Joy the Lord has returned. What's a royal to our bleeders and muters? Praise be to bear witness. Sanctuary, it's his. The lord of terror has returned."

## What This Means for Players

For the dedicated **Diablo** community, the announcement of **Diablo 5** is a monumental event, solidifying the franchise's future for years to come. The decision to set the game entirely post-apocalypse is a significant narrative departure that has sparked immediate discussion and speculation. Players are eager to see how Blizzard interprets a world reshaped by the events of **Diablo 4**, and what new challenges and horrors await them. The extended development window, targeting 2029, suggests an ambition for a polished and expansive experience, potentially leveraging new technologies to deliver the most immersive Sanctuary yet. The simultaneous announcements regarding **Diablo 4**'s continued support and the Switch 2 port show Blizzard's commitment to engaging players across multiple fronts.

## What's Next

While **Diablo 5** is slated for Spring 2029, more details are expected to emerge in the coming years. Players can sign up for future updates on the official **Diablo 5** website. Meanwhile, the current focus remains on **Diablo 4**'s ongoing seasons and upcoming content, including The Amazon class pack in 2027.

content_raw: Diablo 5, a brand-new mainline entry in Blizzard’s long-running action RPG series, was announced today at BlizzCon 2026. A short teaser during today's BlizzCon’s opening ceremony shows the return of the Lord of Terror, one century after the events of Diablo 4. The Diablo development team also revealed that Diablo 5 will release in Spring 2029, a full 6 years after the release of Diablo 4, and more than three decades after the series first launched. Diablo 5’s story is confirmed to take place a full century after the events of Diablo 4, and will be the first game in the series that is set entirely post-apocalypse. BlizzCon 2026 also saw more Diablo news, including The Amazon - a new class pack coming to Diablo 4 in 2027, word that the Diablo 4 Collection coming to Nintendo Switch 2, and Season 15, a broad playable look-back at the history of the Diablo franchise, which is available now.
